title: Avoiding Reverse Fall on Waste Pipes
description: One of the most critical errors in drainage installation is failing to maintain consistent gravity fall on horizontal waste pipes. When a waste pipe lacks proper slope or, worse, sags backward, wastewater stagnates, allowing suspended solids to settle and eventually form a severe clog. Proper installation requires continuous downward momentum toward the main drain. Always check your hanger spacing and support every section securely to prevent sagging over time. Understanding how wastewater travels helps you diagnose chronic slow drains and ensures your installations stand the test of time.
